prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: High fidelity mobile app visual redesign proposal for FoodJury. This is a concept, with fictional sample food choices.
Input image: reference character sheet. Use ONLY its large orange friendly gavel character as the provisional mascot, preserving face, simple orange T-shaped silhouette and ivory collar. Do not put the whole sheet or its labels in the UI.
Create a highly polished landscape design board with exactly THREE large mobile app screens side by side, straight-on, crisp and readable, no perspective, no physical hardware mockup or hands. Each screen a realistic tall phone proportion and equal size. Use a soft warm neutral board outside the screen panels and tiny labels "HOME", "BUILD A CASE", "THE VERDICT" above. Screens fill nearly all the canvas height.
Art direction: premium contemporary neighborhood restaurant menu meets witty food courtroom, warm cream #FFF8F0 backgrounds, near-black warm navy #202332 type, burnt orange #C84B27 actions, a little pale peach. Confident rounded editorial serif for the main expressive headlines only; exceptionally clean sans-serif for controls and readable supporting text. Use elegant spacious hierarchy, consistent 22px inset margins, very subtle hairline borders, restrained 20px card corners, no heavy black borders, no hard offset shadows, no gradients, no neon, no glass. Keep a warm adult personality. Everything meticulously aligned. Avoid filler dashboard metrics, badges, score percentages, or excessive decoration. Food itself must feel appetizing.
SCREEN 1 HOME:
Top native status line 9:41, compact "FoodJury" wordmark with small settings icon.
Large left-aligned serif headline "Dinner indecision?" below small "GOOD EVENING".
Secondary line "Bring your options. I'll make the call."
One warm pale peach hero area with the friendly orange gavel mascot, simplified from reference, medium size rather than overwhelming the full screen. Small casual speech label "Court is in session."
Strong full-width burnt orange button with ivory label "Start a food case" and small arrow.
Section "Recent verdicts" with small "View all" action. Two very clean compact rows with tiny appetizing food photo thumbnails, "Birria tacos" / "Fun · Yesterday" and "Salmon bowl" / "Quick · Monday". Thin separators. Quiet bottom navigation "Court" and "History".
SCREEN 2 BUILD A CASE:
Status line 9:41, subtle back arrow and top "New case".
Large serif heading "What's on the table?"
Small explanation "Add 2–5 options. Photos are optional."
Two clean cream-white food option cards, each horizontal with a tasteful appetizing photo thumbnail at left, a food name and one short note: "Birria tacos" / "Crispy, cheesy, a little messy." and "Salmon bowl" / "Fresh, bright, and filling." Each tiny edit icon on right.
Quiet outline button "+ Add another option".
Section label "What matters tonight?" followed by four spacious 2x2 goal chips "Fun", "Healthy", "Fit", "Quick". Only "Fun" selected with pale orange fill and clear check mark; other chips neutral. One small line "Judge Bite will weigh your options."
At bottom a full-width burnt orange button "Let the judge decide".
SCREEN 3 VERDICT:
Status line 9:41, back arrow and "The verdict".
Small eyebrow "CASE CLOSED", large warm serif headline "Tacos take it."
Large rounded-corner appetizing close-up food photograph of three birria tacos on a neutral plate with lime and consommé, no text on photograph.
Tiny pale orange chip "Best for Fun".
A concise reasoning section with a small mascot avatar and "Judge Bite's ruling", then clearly legible short text "Crispy edges, rich flavor, and a little mess. Tonight calls for tacos."
Secondary expandable text row "See the other option" with chevron.
Bottom full-width burnt orange button "Share verdict", and below quiet text action "Start another case".
Keep all important content within the screen, no clipping. All type is plausible real mobile UI size, no giant mockup text or tiny unreadable placeholder writing. This should look like a thoughtfully designed, shippable consumer app, not a web dashboard.
